Agent-to-Agent Protocol
Agent 间协议（A2A）

In “Multiagent Systems” on page 295 we introduced multiagent systems where specialized agents collaborate on complex tasks. A planner agent might break down a feature request into smaller steps, delegate code generation to a coder agent, and send the resulting implementation to a tester agent for validation. Each agent brings domain expertise, but without a standard way to communicate, these systems become brittle and framework locked.

在 295 页“多智能体系统”一节中，我们介绍了由专业智能体协作完成复杂任务的多智能体系统。一个规划智能体可能把功能需求拆成更小的步骤，把代码生成委派给编码智能体，再把得到的实现交给测试智能体验证。每个智能体都带来领域专长，但如果没有标准通信方式，这些系统会变得脆弱且被框架锁定。

As of early 2026, most multiagent frameworks still use their own internal coordination mechanisms. LangGraph uses in-process Python function calls to pass control between agents. CrewAI implements custom REST endpoints for agent communication. This fragmentation creates operational challenges when you need distributed agents to work across cluster boundaries, when different teams use different frameworks, or when compliance requires auditable communication between agents. You cannot easily connect a LangGraph planner to a CrewAI coder, and you cannot monitor or enforce policies on agent interactions that happen inside framework-specific abstractions.

截至 2026 年初，大多数多智能体框架仍使用各自内部的协调机制。LangGraph 用进程内 Python 函数调用来在智能体之间传递控制流。CrewAI 实现了自定义 REST 端点用于智能体通信。当你需要分布式智能体跨集群边界协作、不同团队使用不同框架、或合规要求智能体之间通信可审计时，这种碎片化会带来运维挑战。你无法轻松把一个 LangGraph 规划器接到 CrewAI 编码器上，也无法监控或对发生在框架专属抽象内部的智能体交互执行策略。

The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol emerged to solve this coordination problem. A2A standardizes how agents discover each other's capabilities, delegate tasks, track progress, and stream results. It provides a common language for multiagent systems, much like HTTP provides a common language for web services. In August 2025, IBM's Agent Communication Protocol (ACP) merged into A2A under the Linux Foundation, consolidating the two major agent-to-agent communication initiatives. ACP brought a RESTful approach to agent communication (complementing MCP's JSON-RPC), and its integration into A2A strengthens the protocol as the unified standard for agent interoperability.

Agent-to-Agent（A2A）协议应运而生，解决这一协调问题。A2A 标准化了智能体如何发现彼此能力、委派任务、跟踪进度和流式返回结果。它为多智能体系统提供了一种共同语言，就像 HTTP 为 Web 服务提供共同语言一样。2025 年 8 月，IBM 的 Agent Communication Protocol（ACP）在 Linux Foundation 下并入 A2A，把这两大智能体间通信倡议合并。ACP 为智能体通信带来了 RESTful 风格（与 MCP 的 JSON-RPC 互补），它并入 A2A 进一步巩固了该协议作为智能体互操作统一标准的地位。

A2A complements MCP
A2A 与 MCP 互补

Before diving into A2A itself, we should clarify how it relates to MCP, covered in the previous section. Both are standards for connecting AI components, but they serve different purposes and operate at different levels of abstraction.

在深入 A2A 本身之前，我们应先厘清它与上一节 MCP 的关系。两者都是连接 AI 组件的标准，但用途不同，工作在不同抽象层次。

MCP connects agents to tools and data sources, and it follows a synchronous request-response pattern: the agent sends a typed request, the tool performs an operation, and the tool returns a result. This makes MCP ideal for integrating agents with the operational environment around them.

MCP 把智能体连接到工具和数据源，它遵循同步请求-响应模式：智能体发送一个带类型的请求，工具执行一个操作，工具返回结果。这使 MCP 非常适合把智能体与它周围的运行环境集成起来。

Footnote 2: As of early 2026, MCP has added asynchronous task execution, further narrowing the functional gap with A2A. With both protocols now under Linux Foundation governance, they are positioned as complementary layers, but it is not implausible that MCP's adoption advantage will eventually absorb A2A's functionality.脚注 2：截至 2026 年初，MCP 已加入异步任务执行，进一步缩小了与 A2A 的功能差距。两个协议现在都在 Linux Foundation 治理下，被定位为互补层；但 MCP 的采用优势最终吞噬 A2A 的功能，也并非不可能。

原书第 367 页

A2A, in contrast, connects agents to other agents. When one agent needs another agent to perform work that requires reasoning, planning, or iteration, it uses A2A to delegate that task. The receiving agent is not a passive tool but rather an autonomous system that can break down the request, call its own tools, and make decisions about how to proceed. A2A follows an asynchronous task delegation model with lifecycle tracking: the requesting agent submits a task, receives a task identifier, and polls or subscribes to status updates as the receiving agent works through the problem. This asynchronous nature reflects the reality that agents often need time to reason and iterate before producing results.

相比之下，A2A 把智能体连接到其他智能体。当一个智能体需要另一个智能体执行需要推理、规划或迭代的工作时，它用 A2A 委派该任务。接收方智能体不是被动工具，而是一个自主系统：它能拆解请求、调用自己的工具，并决定下一步如何进行。A2A 遵循带生命周期跟踪的异步任务委派模型：请求方智能体提交一个任务，拿到一个任务标识符，然后在接收方智能体处理问题期间轮询或订阅状态更新。这种异步特性反映了现实：智能体在产出结果前往往需要时间推理和迭代。

You could model another agent as an “MCP tool” and use MCP for inter-agent communication. This approach works for simple delegation scenarios where you just need to hand off a request and wait for a response. However, treating agents as tools loses the richer semantics that A2A provides. MCP does not yet have a concept of agent capability discovery, so you cannot programmatically find agents with specific skills. MCP has no task lifecycle tracking, so you cannot monitor long-running agent work or cancel tasks that are no longer needed. Designed as a frontend for classical deterministic APIs, MCP does not support streaming of intermediate reasoning steps, so you cannot observe an agent's progress as it works through a multistep plan when implemented as an MCP server.

你可以把另一个智能体建模成一个“MCP 工具”，用 MCP 做智能体间通信。这种方式在简单委派场景下可行——你只需交出请求并等待响应。然而，把智能体当工具会丢失 A2A 提供的更丰富语义。MCP 还没有智能体能力发现的概念，因此你无法以编程方式找到具备特定技能的智能体。MCP 没有任务生命周期跟踪，因此你无法监控长时间运行的智能体工作，也无法取消不再需要的任务。MCP 被设计成面向经典确定性 API 的前端，不支持流式返回中间推理步骤，因此当智能体以 MCP 服务器实现时，你无法观察它在多步计划中的进展。

The best practice is to use A2A for cross-agent orchestration and MCP for tool integration within each agent. This separation of concerns keeps your architecture composable. Each agent uses MCP to connect to its own set of tools and data sources, and uses A2A to coordinate with other agents when the work requires delegation to another reasoning system. You can upgrade, replace, or scale individual agents without disrupting the tool integrations, and you can change tool implementations without affecting agent coordination.

最佳实践是：用 A2A 做跨智能体编排，用 MCP 在每个智能体内部做工具集成。这种关注点分离让架构保持可组合。每个智能体用 MCP 连接自己那一组工具和数据源，当工作需要委派给另一个推理系统时，用 A2A 与其他智能体协调。你可以升级、替换或扩缩单个智能体而不打乱工具集成，也可以更换工具实现而不影响智能体协调。

A2A in a Nutshell
A2A 一览

A2A builds on standard web protocols: HTTP for transport, JSON for data representation, and JSON-RPC for structured method calls. This makes it approachable for teams already familiar with REST APIs and service-to-service communication. The protocol introduces three core concepts that enable robust multiagent coordination.

A2A 构建在标准 Web 协议之上：HTTP 做传输、JSON 做数据表示、JSON-RPC 做结构化方法调用。这让熟悉 REST API 和服务间通信的团队容易上手。该协议引入了三个核心概念，以实现健壮的多智能体协调。

The first concept is the agent card, a JSON document that describes what an agent can do. An agent card lists the skills the agent offers, the input formats it accepts, the output formats it produces, and the protocol versions it supports. This serves the same role as an OpenAPI specification for a REST API: it tells other agents what to expect when they interact with this agent. A simplified agent card for a code reviewer is shown in Example 9-13.

第一个概念是 agent card（智能体卡片），一个描述智能体能做什么的 JSON 文档。agent card 列出该智能体提供的技能、接受的输入格式、产出的输出格式，以及支持的协议版本。它的作用相当于 REST API 的 OpenAPI 规范：告诉其他智能体与这个智能体交互时可以期待什么。例 9-13 给出了一个代码评审智能体的简化 agent card。

原书第 368 页

Example 9-13. Agent card for code reviewer in the A2A protocol

{
  "agent_id": "code-reviewer",
  "skills": ["code_review", "security_scan"],
  "input_modes": ["text/plain", "application/json"],
  "output_modes": ["application/json"],
  "protocols": ["a2a/v1"]
}

When a planner agent needs to delegate a code review, it can query a discovery service for agents that offer the code_review skill, retrieve the agent card, and verify that the reviewer accepts the input format the planner wants to send.

当一个规划智能体需要委派代码评审时，它可以查询发现服务，找到提供 code_review 技能的智能体，取回其 agent card，并确认该评审器接受规划器想发送的输入格式。

The second concept is the task lifecycle, a state machine that tracks delegated work from creation to completion. When an agent delegates a task to another agent, it submits the task with an input payload and receives a task identifier in return. The task moves through defined states: created when first submitted, in_progress when the receiving agent starts work, and eventually completed, failed, or cancelled, depending on the outcome. The requesting agent can poll the /task endpoint to check status, or subscribe to updates if the receiving agent supports push notifications. This lifecycle model handles long-running work gracefully and provides clear visibility into what each agent is doing at any moment.

第二个概念是任务生命周期，一个从创建到完成跟踪被委派工作的状态机。当一个智能体把任务委派给另一个智能体时，它带一个输入 payload 提交任务，并收到一个任务标识符。任务在若干定义好的状态间迁移：刚提交时为 created，接收方智能体开始工作时为 in_progress，最终根据结果变为 completed、failed 或 cancelled。请求方智能体可以轮询 /task 端点查看状态，或者在接收方支持推送通知时订阅更新。这种生命周期模型优雅地处理长时间运行的工作，并在任意时刻清晰可见每个智能体在做什么。

The third concept is artifact streaming, a mechanism for passing large or incremental results between agents without blocking. As an agent works on a task, it can stream partial results back to the requester. A documentation agent generating a multisection report might stream each section as it completes, allowing downstream agents to begin processing early sections while later sections are still being generated. Artifact streaming reduces end-to-end latency in multiagent pipelines and provides visibility into agent progress even before the task is fully complete.

第三个概念是 artifact 流式传输，一种在智能体之间非阻塞地传递大型或增量结果的机制。当智能体处理任务时，可以把部分结果流式回传给请求方。一个生成多章节报告的文档智能体可以在每完成一章时就流式发出，让下游智能体在后面章节还在生成时就开始处理前面的章节。artifact 流式传输降低了多智能体流水线的端到端延迟，并在任务完全完成之前就让你看到智能体进展。

The key insight is that tasks have lifecycles independent of HTTP requests. A planner can submit a task and disconnect, then reconnect later to check progress. This decoupling makes A2A robust in distributed environments where network partitions or agent restarts might occur during long-running work.

关键洞见在于：任务拥有独立于 HTTP 请求的生命周期。规划器可以提交任务后断开连接，稍后再重连查看进度。这种解耦让 A2A 在分布式环境中更健壮——长时间运行的工作期间可能发生网络分区或智能体重启。

Running A2A on Kubernetes
在 Kubernetes 上运行 A2A

From a Kubernetes perspective, A2A enables a deployment model where each agent runs as a separate deployment with its own service endpoint. This mirrors the microservices pattern we have been applying throughout this book, now extended to autonomous reasoning systems.

从 Kubernetes 视角看，A2A 支持这样一种部署模型：每个智能体作为独立的 deployment 运行，拥有自己的 service 端点。这呼应了本书贯穿始终的微服务模式，现在把它扩展到了自主推理系统。

Agents scale independently based on their workload characteristics. A code reviewer agent with high request volume might run with more replicas than a planner agent with lower concurrency demands. This independence extends to release cadences, allowing improvements to the reviewer without touching the planner or tester. On the security side, NetworkPolicies restrict which agents can communicate with each other, implementing defense-in-depth for your multiagent system. For resilience, circuit breakers via service mesh policies enable graceful degradation when an agent becomes unhealthy, preventing cascading failures through the system.

智能体根据各自的负载特征独立扩缩。请求量大的代码评审智能体可以比并发需求低的规划智能体跑更多副本。这种独立性还延伸到发布节奏：改进评审器时不必动规划器或测试器。在安全侧，NetworkPolicy 限制哪些智能体可以互相通信，为你的多智能体系统实现深度防御。在韧性侧，通过服务网格策略配置的断路器能在某个智能体不健康时优雅降级，防止故障在系统中级联蔓延。

原书第 369 页

The agent card becomes a contract that you can validate at deployment time. Before rolling out a new version of an agent, you can verify that its agent card remains compatible with existing consumers. If a new reviewer agent drops support for text/plain input, but all your planners send plain text diffs, you catch that incompatibility before deployment rather than discovering it in production.

agent card 成了一份你可以在部署时校验的契约。在发布某个智能体的新版本之前，你可以验证它的 agent card 是否仍与现有消费方兼容。如果新评审智能体不再支持 text/plain 输入，而你所有规划器都发送纯文本 diff，你就能在部署前发现这种不兼容，而不是到生产中才暴露。

Task lifecycle tracking makes multiagent operations observable. You can instrument your monitoring stack to track which tasks are stuck in the in_progress state for too long, which agents have high failure rates, and where bottlenecks occur in multistep workflows. This visibility is crucial for debugging and optimizing agent systems at scale.

任务生命周期跟踪让多智能体运维可观测。你可以在监控栈上埋点，跟踪哪些任务长时间卡在 in_progress 状态、哪些智能体失败率高、多步工作流的瓶颈出现在哪里。这种可见性对大规模智能体系统的排障和优化至关重要。

With agents deployed as independent services, MCP and A2A solve the integration challenges—connecting agents to tools and to each other. However, they assume the agents themselves are stateless services that can be scaled horizontally behind a load balancer. This assumption breaks down the moment you deploy a conversational agent that needs to remember context across multiple turns. The protocols handle communication; however, you still need to solve persistence.

当智能体作为独立服务部署后，MCP 和 A2A 解决了集成挑战——把智能体连接到工具、连接到彼此。然而，它们假设智能体本身是无状态服务，可以在负载均衡器后水平扩缩。一旦你部署一个需要跨多轮记住上下文的会话式智能体，这个假设就失效了。协议处理了通信，但你仍需解决持久化问题。

Agent State Management
Agent 状态管理

When you deploy agents on Kubernetes, one of the first challenges you'll encounter is statefulness. Unlike traditional REST APIs where each request is independent, agents are conversational by nature. They need to remember in their state what the user asked three turns ago, what documents they've already retrieved, and what intermediate conclusions they've drawn. Consider a customer support agent that helps a user troubleshoot a database connection issue. The first turn identifies the database type. The second turn asks for error logs. The third turn suggests a specific configuration change based on the context from the previous two turns. This accumulated memory is fundamental to the agent's ability to provide useful assistance.

在 Kubernetes 上部署智能体时，你遇到的首要挑战之一就是有状态性。与传统 REST API 中每个请求相互独立不同，智能体本质上是会话式的。它们需要在状态中记住用户三轮前提了什么、已经检索过哪些文档、得出过哪些中间结论。以一个帮助用户排查数据库连接问题的客服智能体为例。第一轮识别数据库类型，第二轮索要错误日志，第三轮根据前两轮的上下文建议一个具体的配置改动。这种累积记忆是智能体提供有用帮助的根本。

The statefulness challenge raises several operational questions. Where does this state live, and how do you maintain it across restarts? How do you scale horizontally when each agent instance needs access to conversation history? In this section, we'll walk through the patterns that solve these challenges, from simple in-memory approaches suitable for development, to production-grade solutions using key-value (KV) stores and databases.

有状态挑战带来了若干运维问题。状态存在哪里？如何在重启后保留它？当每个智能体实例都需要访问会话历史时，如何水平扩缩？本节将逐一讲解解决这些挑战的模式——从适合开发的简单内存方式，到使用键值（KV）存储和数据库的生产级方案。

原书第 370 页

State Storage Patterns
状态存储模式

Agent state falls into two categories: short-term memory holds the active conversation context for current sessions, while long-term memory persists user preferences, historical interactions, and learned patterns across sessions. Short-term memory needs low-latency access during active conversations, while long-term memory supports analytics, personalization, and audit requirements.

智能体状态分两类：短期记忆保存当前会话的活跃对话上下文，长期记忆则跨会话持久化用户偏好、历史交互和学到的模式。短期记忆需要在活跃对话中低延迟访问，长期记忆则支撑分析、个性化和审计需求。

The simplest approach to managing short-term memory is keeping everything in RAM within the pod. Your agent maintains a dictionary, mapping session IDs to conversation histories and storing the entire context in RAM. This works beautifully during development and testing because there's no external dependency to configure. You can iterate quickly without thinking about state infrastructure. However, this approach has significant limitations in production. If the pod restarts—whether due to a deployment, node failure, or resource pressure—all conversation state is lost. Users mid-conversation will effectively start from scratch with no memory of what they've discussed. You also can't scale horizontally because each pod has its own isolated state. If a load balancer sends consecutive requests from the same user to different pods, the conversation context won't follow them.

管理短期记忆最简单的方式是把一切都放在 pod 内的 RAM 里。你的智能体维护一个字典，把会话 ID 映射到对话历史，把整个上下文存在内存中。这在开发和测试期间非常顺手，因为没有外部依赖要配置。你可以快速迭代，而不必操心状态基础设施。然而这种方式在生产中有明显局限。如果 pod 重启——无论是因为部署、节点故障还是资源压力——所有对话状态都会丢失。对话进行到一半的用户实际上会从零开始，完全不记得之前聊过什么。你也无法水平扩缩，因为每个 pod 都有自己隔离的状态。如果负载均衡器把同一用户的连续请求发到不同 pod，对话上下文不会跟着走。

For production deployments, the most common pattern for short-term memory is using a distributed key-value (KV) store like Redis. KV stores give you fast in-memory access with persistence guarantees, allowing session state to survive pod restarts. The pattern is straightforward: when a user starts a conversation, you generate a session ID and use it as a key in your KV store. After each turn, you serialize the conversation state and save it back with a time-to-live (TTL) that matches your session expiration policy.

对于生产部署，短期记忆最常见的模式是使用像 Redis 这样的分布式键值（KV）存储。KV 存储既提供快速的内存访问，又有持久化保证，让会话状态在 pod 重启后仍在。模式很直接：当用户开始一段对话时，你生成一个会话 ID，把它用作 KV 存储的键。每轮之后，你把对话状态序列化，按与会话过期策略匹配的存活时间（TTL）存回去。

Figure 9-7 illustrates how agents manage state across the request lifecycle, using KV stores for session state and optionally integrating with databases for long-term memory.

图 9-7 展示了智能体如何在请求生命周期中管理状态：用 KV 存储保存会话状态，并可选地与数据库集成以提供长期记忆。

On the Kubernetes side, you'll typically deploy your state store as a StatefulSet with a PersistentVolume to ensure the data survives pod restarts. This gives you several important benefits. State survives pod restarts because of the persisted data. You can scale your agent pods horizontally because they all connect to the same state store. A time-to-live mechanism automatically cleans up abandoned sessions without manual intervention when they are inactive for a certain time.

在 Kubernetes 侧，你通常把状态存储以 StatefulSet 加 PersistentVolume 的方式部署，以确保数据在 pod 重启后存活。这带来几个重要好处：由于数据持久化，状态在 pod 重启后仍在；你可以水平扩缩智能体 pod，因为它们都连到同一个状态存储；TTL 机制会在会话闲置一段时间后自动清理被遗弃的会话，无需人工干预。

原书第 371 页

Choosing Between Key-Value Stores and Databases
在 KV 存储与数据库之间选择

Production systems often combine both KV stores and databases, mapping them to the two types of agent memory. KV stores handle short-term memory (active session state), while databases handle long-term memory (historical patterns and audit trails). Understanding when to use which storage layer prevents both over-engineering (adding a database when you do not need one) and under-engineering (hitting KV store limitations as requirements evolve).

生产系统常常同时使用 KV 存储和数据库，把它们映射到两种智能体记忆。KV 存储处理短期记忆（活跃会话状态），数据库处理长期记忆（历史模式和审计轨迹）。理解何时用哪一层存储，能既避免过度工程（不需要数据库时硬加一个），也避免工程不足（需求演进后撞上 KV 存储的局限）。

This part is already explained in very similar wording in the previous subsection.

这一部分已在上一小节中用非常相近的措辞讲过。

For pure conversational agents where each session is independent and you do not need to query across sessions, a KV store for short-term memory alone is sufficient. Databases become necessary when you need long-term memory capabilities beyond single-session retrieval. SQL databases let you write queries that span sessions: “Show me all conversations where users mentioned pricing concerns in the last week” or “What percentage of sessions escalated to human support?” This cross-session analysis is impossible with a KV store's key-value model. Databases also provide the durability and immutability required for compliance and audit trails. When you need to prove what recommendations your agent made six months ago for regulatory purposes, that data must live in a backed-up database that can be queried and that has proper retention policies.

对于纯会话式智能体（每个会话相互独立、不需要跨会话查询），仅用 KV 存储做短期记忆就足够了。当你需要超出单会话检索的长期记忆能力时，数据库就变得必要。SQL 数据库让你能写跨会话的查询：“列出过去一周用户提到价格顾虑的所有对话”，或“升级到人工支持的会话占比是多少？”这种跨会话分析用 KV 存储的键值模型做不到。数据库还提供合规和审计轨迹所需的持久性与不可变性。当你需要出于监管目的证明智能体六个月前给出过什么建议时，这些数据必须存在一个有备份、可查询、并有恰当保留策略的数据库里。

The pattern that works in production combines both layers. Every request reads and writes short-term memory (session state) through your KV store. When you need to persist something to long-term memory—audit logs, user preferences, or insights for analytics—you write that to a database, typically asynchronously so it does not block the user response. When an agent needs context from past sessions stored in long-term memory—perhaps user preferences or historical patterns—you query the database during session initialization and cache the results in short-term memory.

生产中行之有效的模式是两层结合。每个请求都通过 KV 存储读写短期记忆（会话状态）。当你需要把某些内容持久化到长期记忆——审计日志、用户偏好或用于分析的洞见——时，把它写到数据库，通常是异步写，以免阻塞用户响应。当智能体需要长期记忆中存储的过往会话上下文——也许是用户偏好或历史模式——时，在会话初始化期间查询数据库，并把结果缓存到短期记忆里。

原书第 372 页

This layered approach gives you speed and allows queries. Your analytics team can run reports against long-term memory in the database to understand agent behavior patterns. The compliance team can audit conversation logs with proper retention policies and the engineering team can debug issues by querying production data with SQL. Your users get fast responses because the short-term memory-critical path stays in memory.

这种分层方式既给你速度，又允许查询。你的分析团队可以针对数据库中的长期记忆跑报告，了解智能体行为模式；合规团队可以按恰当保留策略审计对话日志；工程团队可以用 SQL 查询生产数据来排障。用户获得快速响应，因为短期记忆这一关键路径始终在内存中。

For simple agents—internal tools, development environments, or purely ephemeral conversations—start with a KV store for short-term memory alone. Add a database for long-term memory when you hit one of these requirements: regulatory compliance that demands immutable audit trails, analytics needs that require cross-session queries, or data retention policies that exceed what you want to keep in your KV store. The KV store remains your short-term memory performance layer; the database becomes your long-term memory durability and querying layer.

对于简单智能体——内部工具、开发环境或纯临时性对话——先用 KV 存储做短期记忆即可。当遇到以下任一需求时再加数据库做长期记忆：要求不可变审计轨迹的监管合规、需要跨会话查询的分析需求，或保留策略超出你想在 KV 存储中保留范围的数据保留要求。KV 存储始终是你的短期记忆性能层；数据库则成为你的长期记忆持久层与查询层。

Checkpointing for Long-Running Agents
长时间运行智能体的检查点

Some agents execute workflows that span hours or even days. Consider a research agent that needs to review hundreds of documents, extract key findings, and synthesize a comprehensive report. Or you can use a testing agent that runs a suite of experiments, analyzes results, and generates recommendations. These long-running processes need a different pattern: checkpointing for saving the intermediate results.

有些智能体执行的工作流要持续数小时甚至数天。设想一个研究智能体，需要审阅数百份文档、提取关键发现并综合成一份综合报告；或者一个测试智能体，跑一组实验、分析结果并给出建议。这些长时间运行的过程需要另一种模式：保存中间结果的检查点（checkpointing）。

The idea is simple. After completing each major step in the workflow, the agent saves a checkpoint containing its current state and progress. If the pod is evicted or crashes, the agent can resume from the most recent checkpoint rather than starting from scratch. This pattern is especially valuable on Kubernetes where pods are ephemeral and can be rescheduled at any time.

思路很简单。在工作流每完成一个主要步骤后，智能体保存一个包含其当前状态和进度的检查点。如果 pod 被驱逐或崩溃，智能体可以从最近的检查点恢复，而不是从零开始。这种模式在 Kubernetes 上尤其有价值，因为 pod 是临时性的、随时可能被重新调度。

Example 9-14 provides a basic checkpoint implementation, ignoring any user context.

例 9-14 给出一个基本检查点实现（暂不考虑任何用户上下文）。

Example 9-14. Simple checkpoint algorithm

import json
from pathlib import Path

def save_checkpoint(step: int, state: dict):
    # Store checkpoints on a PersistentVolume mounted at /data
    checkpoint_dir = Path("/data/checkpoints")
    checkpoint_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    # Save state as JSON with a sequential step number
    (checkpoint_dir / f"step_{step:03d}.json").write_text(json.dumps(state))

def load_latest_checkpoint() -> tuple[int, dict]:
    checkpoint_dir = Path("/data/checkpoints")
    # Find all existing checkpoints and sort by filename
    checkpoints = sorted(checkpoint_dir.glob("step_*.json"))

    if not checkpoints:
        # Start from scratch if no checkpoints exist
        return 0, {}
    latest = checkpoints[-1]
    step = int(latest.stem.split("_")[1])
    return step, json.loads(latest.read_text())
原书第 373 页

In your Kubernetes job manifest, you'd configure the pod with restartPolicy: OnFailure and mount a PersistentVolumeClaim to /data. When the pod starts, it calls load_latest_checkpoint() to determine where to resume. After each significant step—perhaps after processing a batch of documents or completing a phase of analysis—it calls save_checkpoint() to record progress. If the pod fails or is evicted, Kubernetes restarts it, and the agent picks up exactly where it left off.

在你的 Kubernetes job 清单中，把 pod 配置为 restartPolicy: OnFailure，并把一个 PersistentVolumeClaim 挂载到 /data。pod 启动时调用 load_latest_checkpoint() 确定从哪里恢复。每完成一个重要步骤——也许是处理完一批文档或完成一个分析阶段——就调用 save_checkpoint() 记录进度。如果 pod 失败或被驱逐，Kubernetes 重启它，智能体精确地从上次停下的地方继续。

The checkpoint directory becomes a valuable debugging tool as well. You can inspect the intermediate states to understand what the agent was thinking at each step. If the final output is unexpected, you can trace back through the checkpoints to identify where the reasoning went astray. This visibility is crucial for complex agents where the decision chain might involve dozens of steps.

检查点目录同时也是宝贵的调试工具。你可以检查中间状态，了解智能体每一步在想什么。如果最终输出出乎意料，可以沿着检查点回溯，找出推理从哪里开始跑偏。这种可见性对决策链可能涉及几十个步骤的复杂智能体至关重要。

With MCP for tool integration, A2A for agent coordination, and state management patterns for persistence, you have the foundational components for deploying agentic applications on Kubernetes. These building blocks address the core operational challenges: secure communication between agents and tools, standardized inter-agent protocols, and stateful conversation management across distributed pods.

有了用于工具集成的 MCP、用于智能体协调的 A2A，以及用于持久化的状态管理模式，你就拥有了在 Kubernetes 上部署智能体应用的基础组件。这些积木解决了核心运维挑战：智能体与工具间的安全通信、标准化的智能体间协议，以及跨分布式 pod 的有状态对话管理。

Lessons Learned
本章小结

Running agentic applications in production requires treating them as autonomous systems that reason, iterate, and make decisions based on natural language input. Unlike deterministic microservices with predictable failure modes, agents exhibit unique characteristics: nondeterminism, multihop reasoning flows, and emergent behaviors that demand different operational approaches.

在生产中运行智能体应用，要求你把它们当作基于自然语言输入进行推理、迭代和决策的自主系统来对待。与失败模式可预测的确定性微服务不同，智能体表现出独特特征：非确定性、多跳推理流和涌现行为，这些都要求不同的运维方式。

Understanding MCP and A2A at the wire level—not just as framework abstractions—gives you the power to debug production issues, implement custom security policies, and build platform services that enforce organization-wide controls.

在协议线（wire）层面理解 MCP 和 A2A——而不只是把它们当作框架抽象——能让你有能力排查生产问题、实现自定义安全策略，并构建执行组织级管控的平台服务。

Several operational principles will save you pain in production:

有几条运维原则能帮你在生产中少踩坑：

  • Choose security patterns based on compliance requirements, not convenience: If you need user-level attribution, use agent impersonation or token exchange regardless of complexity. For zero-trust environments, invest in SPIFFE/SPIRE even though the learning curve is steep. Use service account delegation only when you control both the agent and API, and your compliance posture allows it.如果需要用户级归属，无论多复杂都要用智能体模拟或令牌交换。对于零信任环境，即便学习曲线陡峭也要投入 SPIFFE/SPIRE。只有当你同时控制智能体和 API、且合规姿态允许时，才使用服务账号委派。
  • Externalize state from the beginning: In-memory state will fail the moment you scale horizontally or survive a pod restart. Use a KV store for session state, and implement checkpointing for long-running workflows. Retrofitting state management after scaling to production is painful.内存状态在你水平扩缩或经历 pod 重启时立刻就会失效。用 KV 存储保存会话状态，为长时间运行的工作流实现检查点。等到扩到生产后再补状态管理会非常痛苦。
  • Leverage Kubernetes primitives: Deployments, Services, NetworkPolicies, RBAC, StatefulSets, and Jobs are battle-tested patterns that work just as well for agentic workloads as they do for traditional microservices.Deployment、Service、NetworkPolicy、RBAC、StatefulSet 和 Job 都是久经考验的模式，对智能体负载和对传统微服务同样有效。
  • Start simple: Deploy agents as standard Kubernetes deployments before introducing service meshes or custom operators. Layer complexity only when you hit concrete limitations, not because the architecture looks elegant on a whiteboard. The operational rigor you build now will remain essential regardless of how the technology evolves.在引入服务网格或自定义 operator 之前，先把智能体作为标准 Kubernetes deployment 部署。只有在遇到具体局限时才叠加复杂度，而不是因为架构在白板上看起来优雅。无论技术如何演进，你现在建立的运维严谨性都将始终重要。

The protocols may change, but the need for secure communication, standardized coordination, and persistent state will remain constant.

协议或许会变，但对安全通信、标准化协调和持久状态的需求将始终不变。
